# Discovery Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos renews each combat instant; Awtsmoos.com keeps every identity bright,
so wisdom, fire, water, and earth become tested law instead of decorative light.

## Mission universe

- Establish one shared combat language for affinities, elements, actions, statuses, effectiveness, interruption, diagnostics, and Daas disclosure.
- Preserve staff and sword timing, casting, guard, parry, stamina, equipment statistics, enemy timelines, rewards, regions, streaming, recovery, offline parity, WebGL fallback, compactJs, and canonical CSS.
- Make multiplayer authority own damage, resistance, statuses, interruption, rewards, and persistence.
- Give single-player an explicit local-authority adapter using the same identifiers and rules.
- Connect player actions, enemy actions, HUD, effects, persistence, and tests to the shared definitions.
- Keep optional effects and models outside fallback readiness.

## Competing architectures

### A. Client-first catalog
Fast to prototype, but duplicates server truth and violates authority. Rejected.

### B. Server-only combat domain
Secure, but prevents deterministic local authority and readable client prediction. Rejected.

### C. Shared JSON records with separate evaluators
Portable and build-safe, but needs schema validation and careful CommonJS/ESM adapters. Strong candidate.

### D. Generated client/server modules
Excellent identity parity, but adds generator and stale-artifact risk. Useful only if canonical JSON becomes too awkward.

### E. Shared pure CommonJS package consumed through adapters
Simple for the server, but browser loading and compactJs boundaries may become heavier. Secondary candidate.

## Preferred direction

Use small canonical JSON records in `shared/combat/`, plus focused pure evaluators mirrored through thin ESM and CommonJS adapters. Keep browser-only presentation and server-only authority outside the shared domain. Build diagnostics into authoritative receipts so tests can prove every modifier.

## Hidden obligations

- Save migration for affinity allocation and bounded statuses.
- Anti-replay retention and cleanup.
- Cast cancellation that prevents phantom projectiles.
- Daas payload filtering rather than unrestricted server truth.
- Status cleanup on defeat, region change, reconnect, and despawn.
- Enemy phase changes and Warden readability.
- Accessibility that never relies on color alone.
- Deterministic build manifests and optional-module audits.
- Browser proof for cold, warm, offline, reduced-motion, high-contrast, WebGL failure, and mobile landscape.

## Completion evidence

Completion requires connected production behavior, focused and full test matrices, deterministic builds, real-browser receipts, performance measurements, process cleanup, and a worktree audit that preserves unrelated changes.
